newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 6.

text.p: English wants tough action on Kirton: Prime Minister Jim Bolger may face mutiny from Health Minister Bill English if he fails to take tough action after publication of an Audit Office inquiry into the awarding of a publicity contract to an advertising agency run by Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton's brother-in-law. Page 1.

Jobless number 14,000 more than a year ago survey shows: Unemployment increased again in the June quarter, and Employment Minister Peter McCardle said on Tuesday he did not expect it would fall until next year. Page 2.
More legal action against Banks considered: Former Northland Polytechnic boss Noel Harrison is giving "serious consideration" to issuing further proceedings against Whangarei MP John Banks. Page 2.

Voucher funding fairer, says Creech: One positive aspect of the possibility of funding tertiary study with vouchers, as proposed in a leaked Education Ministry paper, was that every young New Zealander would have the same entitlement to taxpayer funding, Education Minister Wyatt Creech said on Tuesday. Page 3.

China clay operation brings Ceramco back: Lingerie and clay-mining company Ceramco Corporation has pulled itself out of the mire to report a first-quarter unaudited pre-tax profit of $1 million. Page 13.

Money markets still testing monetary policy: Financial markets continued to test the Reserve Bank's monetary policy settings on Tuesday, but stronger than expected jobs data brought the interest rate-exchange rate mix closer to the bank's desired levels. Page 13.

Fund managers less hopeful than Treasury -- IPAC: Fund managers have a less optimistic outlook than the Treasury about the economy in the next three years, according to the latest IPAC fund manager survey. Page 14.
State ownership will end, says TVNZ boss: Television New Zealand boss Chris Anderson predicts the government will not own the network in ten to 15 years' time. Page 15.
Sex-unit fight not over -- residents: Yaldhurst residents vowed on Tuesday night to keep fighting after their area was chosen for the national youth sex abusers' unit. Page 1.
Ernest Adams in windfall: Ernest Adams Ltd looks to have acquired its new Palmerston North manufacturing and distribution site at a fraction of government valuation. Page 27.
DB to axe 12 jobs at Washdyke brewery: DB Breweries will lay off up to 12 staff from its Washdyke Mainland Brewery at Timaru because of the continuing slump in beer consumption. Page 27.
Tertiary profit plan likely to go: Cabinet is likely to turf out a controversial profit making element of a leaked paper urging radical changes to the country's tertiary system.

Control bid rebounds on Power co directors: The latest salvo in the battle for control of Power New Zealand has exploded in the lap of the independent directors of the Takapuna-based electricity company.

Telecom picture changing direction: Outstanding issues such as number portability hampering the development of a competitive telecommunications market will soon cease to be of importance, says visiting telecommunications consultant Howard Anderson.
